# Day-ahead price forecasting backtest: NYISO N.Y.C. zone (generated by scripts/evaluate_predictions.py)

Test period 2023-01-01 to 2024-12-30 (730 days, 17,520 hourly points). Target: day-ahead LBMP, $/MWh. Hyperparameters chosen on 2022 only ({'max_depth': 4, 'n_estimators': 300}). Every model is scored on exactly the same points. SARIMAX estimation failures: {'sarimax': 0, 'sarimax_x_oracle_temp': 0}.

**Read with care.** Models marked *oracle* use the target day's actual temperature (a perfect weather forecast) and are optimistic. No natural-gas, generation-mix or outage data is used. This is a retrospective backtest on one zone and one 2-year window, not a trading result.

## Overall

| model | MAE ($/MWh) | RMSE | bias | rMAE vs seasonal naive | rRMSE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Naive (same hour yesterday) | 6.03 | 13.55 | +0.01 | 0.454 | 0.427 |
| Seasonal naive (same hour last week) [reference] | 13.26 | 31.73 | +0.88 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| SARIMAX(1,0,1)(1,0,1,24), 56-day window | 6.47 | 13.02 | -2.54 | 0.488 | 0.410 |
| SARIMAX + target-day temperature (oracle) | 6.41 | 12.90 | -2.76 | 0.483 | 0.406 |
| XGBoost, prices + calendar (A) | 6.13 | 13.51 | +0.90 | 0.462 | 0.426 |
| XGBoost, + load lags (B) | 6.08 | 13.35 | +0.91 | 0.458 | 0.421 |
| XGBoost, + target-day temperature (C, oracle) | 5.02 | 11.04 | +0.41 | 0.379 | 0.348 |

## Against the strongest simple benchmark: same hour yesterday

The 168-hour seasonal naive is a weak reference here (day-to-day persistence beats weekly persistence), so the rMAE column above flatters every model. The fair test is yesterday's same-hour price:

| model | MAE | rMAE vs yesterday-naive | DM stat vs yesterday-naive | p-value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seasonal naive (same hour last week) [reference] | 13.26 | 2.200 | +4.26 | 2.02e-05 |
| SARIMAX(1,0,1)(1,0,1,24), 56-day window | 6.47 | 1.073 | +2.08 | 0.0371 |
| SARIMAX + target-day temperature (oracle) | 6.41 | 1.063 | +1.75 | 0.0808 |
| XGBoost, prices + calendar (A) | 6.13 | 1.017 | +0.28 | 0.778 |
| XGBoost, + load lags (B) | 6.08 | 1.008 | +0.14 | 0.887 |
| XGBoost, + target-day temperature (C, oracle) | 5.02 | 0.833 | -4.81 | 1.47e-06 |

Negative DM statistic = lower daily MAE than yesterday-naive. Only the oracle-temperature XGBoost clearly beats it on MAE. SARIMAX (no oracle) is slightly WORSE on MAE (though better on RMSE: it forecasts spikes less badly in squared terms), and XGBoost A and B are statistically indistinguishable from it.

## Diebold-Mariano vs seasonal naive (daily mean absolute error, HAC lag 7)

| model | mean daily MAE difference ($/MWh) | DM stat | p-value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Naive (same hour yesterday) | -7.236 | -4.26 | 2.02e-05 |
| SARIMAX(1,0,1)(1,0,1,24), 56-day window | -6.796 | -3.92 | 8.96e-05 |
| SARIMAX + target-day temperature (oracle) | -6.854 | -3.94 | 8.19e-05 |
| XGBoost, prices + calendar (A) | -7.133 | -4.53 | 6.01e-06 |
| XGBoost, + load lags (B) | -7.188 | -4.54 | 5.68e-06 |
| XGBoost, + target-day temperature (C, oracle) | -8.240 | -4.93 | 8.37e-07 |

Negative difference = lower error than seasonal naive. With 730 daily losses and heavy serial correlation, treat p-values as indicative.
